item.title: Weekly 23
item.description:
AI / Models / Agents

Quantization-Aware Healing: a compressed, 4-bit model that outperforms its full-precision original: Multiverse Computing introduces a 4-bit quantization-aware healing method that outperforms a recovered 60B BF16 checkpoint of the same architecture on seven of its nine reported benchmarks. The additional distillation training was not matched, so the result cannot simply be attributed to quantization itself.

Introducing the XGBoost Vector-Leaf Model | XGBoost: An introduction to trees whose leaves output vectors, using shared tree structures for multi-target prediction.

[2608.27370] Puro-2B: Poor Lab’s Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090: An exploration of low-cost small language model training on RTX 5090 GPUs. The best model in v2 cost less than $6,900 to train; the estimate of reaching Qwen2-1.5B performance for about $4,400 comes from fitting scaling laws.

Training frontier knowledge work agents: A 397B RL training guide with SkyRL | Mercor Blog: Mercor shares engineering experience from training a 397B knowledge work agent with SkyRL.

chenglou/sotaku, Sotaku v2 solves 99.12% of a 25,000-puzzle Sudoku benchmark with an 800K-parameter looped transformer trained from scratch: A roughly 800K-parameter looped Transformer trained from scratch to solve Sudoku. The repository reports that Sotaku v2 solves 99.12% of a 25,000-puzzle benchmark using FP32 and 1,024 inference iterations.

Z1T | Transformer-like models for Z1: Sparse Transformer-like models designed for Z1 probabilistic hardware, exploring model and hardware co-design while sharing some training recipes and weights.

GPT-6 Astra on robot arms | Robocurve: Experiments with GPT-6 Astra operating robot arms. Watching this makes me a little more inclined to believe LLMs can solve everything, though what a demo can actually do still comes down to the specific task.

Model guidance | OpenAI API on using Astra.

**Using the model**
- Use the Responses API and set `model: "gpt-6-astra"`
- New capabilities: asynchronous tool calling (set `async: true` on the tool definition), changing instructions mid-turn (WebSocket mid-turn steering), and changing reasoning effort with `configuration_update` in standard single-agent requests (keeping the request-level effort preserves the original prompt prefix)
- `reasoning.effort: "none"` is unsupported; Fast mode is unavailable with EU data residency

**Migration notes**
- If you previously used `none` / `minimal`, try `low` first
- Prefer Responses for tool use; Chat Completions is available, but tool calling requires Responses
- Remove `temperature` / `top_p` / `top_logprobs` (and the corresponding logprobs)
- When migrating from GPT-5.5 or earlier, update caching: `prompt_cache_retention` → `prompt_cache_options.ttl: "30m"`

**Prompt tuning (the most practical part)**
1. **Initiative**: It tends to ask more follow-up questions by default. To have it finish the work autonomously, explicitly say “infer intent, bias toward action, and don't stop at acknowledging capability or delivering partial work.” Produce a reviewable result before asking for approval.
2. **Instruction priority**: It is more sensitive to skills / `AGENTS.md`; state that “user instructions take precedence over skills.” If it gets stuck, have it quote the specific skill rule.
3. **Writing style**: It tends toward lists, tables, and stock phrases by default. If you want prose, specify paragraphs first, fewer nested lists, and no slop (delve, Bottom Line, X not Y, etc.).
4. **Subagents**: It may delegate too little by default; specify when to delegate in parallel for multi-agent work.
5. **Testing**: It tends to overtest code. For small changes, state “don't write tests that mirror the implementation for reversible, low-impact changes.”

What I focus on in practice: make autonomous execution, writing style, parallel delegation, and testing boundaries explicit to reduce unnecessary questions.

eric provencher on X: “Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra” / X: Eric Provencher discusses writing skills and prompts for Astra.

Mathematics / Research / Learning

The Math of RL - From Policy Gradients to PPO and GRPO: An article on the mathematics of reinforcement learning, from policy gradients to PPO and GRPO.

Introduction to Robotics | IRoM-Lab: Princeton’s introductory robotics course, covering planning, control, state estimation, and robot learning, with drone project assignments.

[Blog] Estimate Diagonal Hessian: An article on estimating diagonal Hessian entries.

Axiom: An AI project for mathematical reasoning and formal proofs.

Announcing FrontierMath Erdős | Epoch AI: Epoch AI introduces a mathematics benchmark of 68 open Erdős problems, using Lean to verify proofs or disproofs.

francesco215.github.io/autoregressive_diffusion/uncertainty.html: Reading on autoregressive diffusion and uncertainty.

\[2609.02867v2\] Magnetized accretion onto rapidly spinning binary black holes: mini-disk thermodynamics, magnetic transport, and dual jets: Numerical simulations of magnetized accretion onto rapidly spinning binary black holes, including mini-disk thermodynamics, magnetic transport, and dual jets.

How Our Data Shaped Neural Architecture Discovery, and How Automation Can Reshape the Future | Core Automation: The article discusses data and the inductive biases of neural network architectures. A randomly initialized, frozen network may still provide useful features, though the linear classifier in the figure was trained.

This makes me wonder: could feature quality across multiple random initializations help screen architectures for a particular type of data in advance? We need to distinguish the quality of the random features themselves from the contribution of subsequent classifier training.

A neural network architecture with a suitable inductive bias may map inputs into a feature space that a simple classifier can use more easily, even when its main weights are random and frozen. Training can further align this initial structure with a specific task.

Figure. Output probabilities of a (linear) logistic classifier trained on a 10,240-dimensional NRF(Neural Random Feature) representation, extracted from identical, randomly initialized ResNet-18 architectures.

Some related papers:

  • [2410.04368] Algorithmic Capabilities of Random Transformers: Freezes the random Transformer body while still optimizing embeddings to activate algorithmic capabilities.
  • [1711.10925] Deep Image Prior: Uses network structure as an image prior without a large training dataset, but still optimizes for an individual image.
  • [1906.04358] Weight Agnostic Neural Networks: Searches for network architectures that perform well across multiple shared weight values.
  • [2206.08464] PRANC: Pseudo RAndom Networks for Compacting deep models: Freezes multiple random basis networks and learns their linear combination coefficients to compress a model.

Theory of Mind as a Central Skill for Researchers: Treats theory of mind as a meta-skill that spans writing, presenting, reviewing, and collaboration. First consider what the audience knows, cares about, and might misinterpret, then decide how much to explain and in what order.

  • When presenting, pair abstract concepts with examples, repeat important points, and avoid large blocks of text. Consider the occasion and the audience.
  • When writing a paper, state your points clearly, give figures and tables detailed explanations, make the whole paper easy to browse, and minimize abbreviations. Avoid adding to the reader’s memory burden.

Arena Physica Thesis: Electromagnetic engineering faces bottlenecks in solvers, fragmented CAE, EDA, testing, and field data, as well as slow and expensive validation feedback. Arena Physica proposes connecting design, simulation, and testing through agent tools, physics foundation models, and real laboratory data.

[2608.29530] The Emergent Symbolic Structure of Artificial Neural Networks: Trained neural networks may implicitly contain symbolic structures, suggesting that symbolism and connectionism may not be entirely opposed. Related paper: [2506.21797] Why Neural Network Can Discover Symbolic Structures with Gradient-based Training: An Algebraic and Geometric Foundation for Neurosymbolic Reasoning

Atlas Fields Studio: Arena Physica’s interactive electromagnetic field prediction demo lets you modify geometry and observe predicted changes in electric and magnetic fields. It is currently labeled Beta.

What is a Smith Chart? | Arena Physica: An introduction to Smith charts in RF engineering.

Programming / Systems / AI Tools

Your First GPUI App - Building a Desktop UI in Rust | Mrsheerluck Blog: An introductory tutorial on building your first desktop application with Rust and GPUI.

emilkowalski/skills: Skills for Designers and Engineers.: Emil Kowalski turns his interface design and animation experience into agent skills covering animation implementation, review, interaction details, and UI prototypes.

DEEIX-AI/DEEIX-Chat: An enterprise AI workspace for model routing, multimodal chat, files, tools, billing, identity, and operations.: An enterprise AI workspace integrating model routing, multimodal conversations, files, tools, billing, and identity management.

Zodex | AI integrated development environment: An AI development workspace built with Rust and Tauri that brings agent conversations, terminals, Git diffs, and rollbacks together. It can import local Codex, Claude Code, and Pi sessions.

Skillry - Agent Skills with Taste: A curated agent skills catalog covering websites, slides, images, and video, with examples and installation instructions.

Polars — Pre-release of Polars 2.0: An introduction to the first release candidate of Polars 2.0, which makes the streaming engine the default for LazyFrame queries and tightens implicit behavior such as type coercion.

get-bb/bb: The agent IDE that builds itself: An agent IDE that can be driven through a desktop app, web interface, CLI, or HTTP API, with live task tracking and steering.

xuanji86/ainiee-translate-skill: An independent, agent-native novel translation system that works similarly to AiNiee without depending on its application, using Claude Code as the translation engine.: A novel translation skill powered by Claude Code that runs independently of the AiNiee application.

mishka-zz/freecad-microwave: FreeCAD workbench for RF and microwave engineering: A FreeCAD workbench for RF and microwave engineering, still in developer preview. Its currently available simulation backend is openEMS.

Blueprint - AI Hardware Design Tool: An AI-assisted hardware design tool.

KiCad - Schematic Capture & PCB Design Software: Open-source software for schematic capture and PCB design.

American-Embedded/kistack: KiStack is a HUMAN WRITTEN bunch of skills for KiCad: Agent skills for KiCad workflows.

TrenTorch: An educational project inspired by Harvard TinyTorch that teaches PyTorch by building a machine learning framework from scratch.

Design Engineer Tools: A tool directory for design engineers.

DesEngs: Resources for Design Engineers · Minimal Website Design Directory — DesEngs: Directories of design engineering resources and minimal website references.

on.design: A resource project for designers, currently accepting sign-ups ahead of launch.

whatships.com — Discover startup launch videos · Tools for making launch videos or mockups— whatships.com: A collection of startup launch videos and tools for making videos and mockups.

jurplel/InstantSpaceSwitcher: Native space switching on macOS with no animation: A tool for disabling macOS’s native Space switching animation.

Omakade | Your games, beautifully together: A local game library for Omarchy that brings together installed games from Steam, Lutris, Heroic, and other sources, then hands launching off to their original platforms.

Download Codenotch — Vinz: A small tool that displays LLM usage beside your Mac’s notch.

thisisgm/flea: A fast, keyboard-first file manager for Omarchy: Quickshell front end, Rust backend.: A keyboard-first file manager for Omarchy with a Quickshell frontend and Rust backend.

omafiles — the file explorer Omarchy was missing: An Omarchy file manager built with Rust and GPUI, integrating search, previews, and Git diffs.

Droppy. Your Mac, just way better.: Brings a file shelf, clipboard, media controls, widgets, and more to your Mac’s notch or a floating Dynamic Island.

Tenacity: An open-source multitrack audio editor and recorder with support for effects plugins, scripting, and signal analysis.

ChatGPT Training: OpenAI’s step-by-step exercises and workflow tutorials for completing practical tasks with ChatGPT Work and Codex.

Which AI Made This?: Compares different models’ responses to the same UI design task and shows the difference made by enabling design skills.

Shortap — Quick tap gestures for your MacBook: A gesture tool that triggers actions when you tap your MacBook’s chassis.

Related open-source projects:

  • Tapify: A menu bar alternative to Knock, supporting single through triple taps for media controls, screenshots, and launching apps
  • Bonk: GPL-licensed, supports up to four consecutive knocks, can trigger Shortcuts / shell commands, and allows different mappings for each app
  • nocnoc: Includes a waveform display and calibration wizard
  • knocker: Distinguishes left, center, and right taps and provides a menu bar interface
  • TapCraft: A Python tool for chassis taps and trackpad zones; accelerometer detection requires sudo, while microphone detection does not

item.title: Weekly 22
item.description:
AI / Models / Agents

How Speculative Decoding Makes LLMs Go Brrr: Explains speculative decoding through its draft-and-parallel-verification loop and compares approaches including independent draft models, Medusa, MTP, EAGLE, DFlash, and DSpark.

Training AI to Paint with Code: Surya Narreddi’s team used reinforcement learning to train a language model to create editable p5.brush JavaScript paintings, focusing on aesthetic rewards built from hand-rated references and pairwise judgments.

deepManifold: Brings together two preprints and related essays that use fixed points, stacked piecewise manifolds, and boundary-conditioned iteration to formulate the geometry, algebra, and computation of neural networks.

GPT-5.6 Sol Runs Doom in Turing Complete: According to the creator’s demo and Tom’s Hardware, GPT-5.6 Sol built a virtual RV32IM CPU called Codex-R32 inside Turing Complete and ran a PureDOOM build on it, although the result was not yet playable.

First Results from Jalapeño: OpenAI reports that its first custom inference chip improved both power efficiency and end-to-end latency against the tested comparison systems while serving several large models in InferenceX; the chip remains in production validation.

GLM-5.3-Flash: Z.ai’s first natively multimodal GLM-5 model uses 320B total parameters, 18B active parameters, a hybrid linear-and-sparse attention architecture, and IndexPool to reduce indexing overhead at long context lengths.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: An open-weight multimodal MoE model and an early preview of the Qwen4 architecture, introducing hybrid GDN–QSA attention, gated residuals, and N-gram embeddings.

Hy4 Preview: Tencent Hunyuan’s open-weight flagship MoE preview has 770B total parameters, activates 49B per token, supports a 1M-token context window, and uses Gated DSA, IndexCache, and iHC.

Mathematics / Research / Learning

Proswit — Interactive Math Articles: A collection of interactive articles on probability, analysis, and foundational mathematics, covering topics such as Bayes’ theorem, the central limit theorem, Brownian motion, and Fourier series.

Could a Neuroscientist Understand a Microprocessor?: Jonas and Kording applied standard neuroscience analyses to a simulated MOS 6502 microprocessor and found that, although the methods produced patterns resembling neuroscience results, they still failed to recover the processor’s known hierarchical structure and functional mechanisms.

Symbolica: A high-performance computer algebra library for Python and Rust that manipulates large symbolic expressions, performs pattern matching, and generates optimized numerical code; its source is viewable, but redistribution and professional use are license-restricted.

s2 CLI and Skill: A read-only Semantic Scholar CLI and agent skill from Hugging Face for searching papers and retrieving references and citations, also used by the Papers with Code chat interface.

You Are NOT Dumb, You Just Lack the Prerequisites: A personal reflection arguing that difficulty with math and other complex subjects often comes from missing prerequisites, and that rebuilding the foundations can make progress possible.

Palomar: A public, searchable registry of Lean formalizations that pins source revisions, checks proofs with Lean, and publishes the exact statements, dependencies, and review comments.

Programming / Systems / AI Tools

GPUIX: Provides React and TypeScript bindings for Zed’s GPUI, rendering native desktop interfaces directly through Metal, DirectX, or Vulkan without Electron or web views.

Scrollbar but Cooler: A front-end experiment that redesigns the web scrollbar while preserving its positional cue and drag interaction.

Lody: A shared workspace for coding-agent teams that connects existing agents and machines through ACP and lets people share sessions and dispatch work from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI.

Archify: A Node.js rendering and validation system for coding agents that deterministically compiles typed JSON IR into self-contained HTML/SVG maps for architecture, workflow, sequence, data flow, and lifecycle diagrams.

Gribouille: A declarative Grammar of Graphics library for Typst, inspired by R’s ggplot2 and Python’s plotnine.

Markdown Graphs: A set of monospace chart and table components installable through shadcn and embeddable in React/MDX, with some components also offering ASCII versions for README files.

Fresh: A terminal text editor built around a zero-configuration, familiar interface, with mouse support, menus, a command palette, LSP, multiple cursors, an integrated terminal, and Git-worktree task orchestration.

Backend from First Principles: An open collection of backend-engineering notes and code examples spanning HTTP, routing, authentication, databases, caching, concurrency, observability, deployment, testing, and event streaming.

How Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, Jobs, and Buckets Power Search on Papers with Code: Hugging Face explains Papers with Code’s hybrid-search architecture: Jobs build paper embeddings offline, Buckets hand off artifacts, Inference Endpoints handle live queries and incremental updates, and RRF combines PostgreSQL full-text search with pgvector retrieval.

macOS / Productivity / Other

omacosy: An Omarchy-style desktop setup for macOS 26 on Apple Silicon, combining AeroSpace or OmniWM, Karabiner, and custom Swift helpers for dwindle tiling, a Super key, a status bar, focus-follows-mouse, and workspace gestures.

OmniWM: An open-source tiling window manager for macOS 26 and Apple Silicon, inspired by Niri and Hyprland and featuring Niri and Dwindle layouts, a workspace overview, a command palette, and optional IPC/CLI control.

deepManifold: Brings together two preprints and related essays that use fixed points, stacked piecewise manifolds, and boundary-conditioned iteration to formulate the geometry, algebra, and computation of neural networks.

item.description:
AI / Models / Agents

math-ai-org/mathcode: A terminal-based mathematical programming agent with Lean integration that can inspect proof goals, search declarations, verify candidate proofs, and complete formal proofs interactively.

Cua: GUI sandboxes and scalable computer clusters for computer-use agents, with both local and hosted deployment options.

Introducing Delta: Zed’s multi-agent coding and review environment, synchronizing code, conversations, and worktrees in real time so people and agents share the same development context.

PyTorch: a reference language: A proposal to retain PyTorch as an executable reference specification, with LLMs generating explicit forward and backward implementations and verifying their equivalence. It also raises the question of whether LLM-written backpropagation could replace automatic differentiation in some settings.

wibus-wee/cradle-app: A desktop-first AI agent management platform for running agents, tracking tasks and sessions, coordinating workflows, and connecting multiple model providers in one place.

Building a distributed training framework from first principles: Umar Jamil explains how to build a distributed model-training framework from first principles; this description is based only on the public video title and author information.

Ornith-1.5: From Self-Scaffolding to Self-Improvement: A model that generates its own training tasks, task scaffolds, and solution trajectories, then uses reinforcement learning to form a continuous self-improvement loop.

Famous Deep Learning Papers: A chronological guide to classic deep-learning papers, summarizing the central problem and historical impact of each work.

CS 8803 - LLM: The course page for Georgia Tech’s Spring 2026 large language models class, collecting lectures, papers, and student presentations on pretraining, reasoning, alignment, and more.

Papers with Code: An index for browsing machine-learning papers, code implementations, and benchmark results by task.

CopilotKit/openbot: An open-source AI coworker platform that gives every agent an isolated browser, files, and tools while recording its decisions and actions.

Machine Studying: Introduces “Machine Studying,” in which agents autonomously develop domain expertise from a document corpus, and explores how to measure that ability with StudyBench.

Hot Take: LLM can ‘jump’: Argues that interconnected knowledge may let models make scientific leaps along paths that differ from human intuition, with implications for safety and continual learning.

[2608.08003] The Spectral Neuron: Introduces explicit nonlinearity through the eigenvalues of an affine matrix, seeking a balance among model expressiveness, coefficient transparency, and shape constraints.

Learn Inference: An interactive introduction to production inference engineering for generative AI, from attention kernels to multi-cloud capacity planning.

The Year in AI Papers: Essential Research from 2025–2026: A collection of important AI papers from 2025–2026, organized by topic, lab, citations, code, and date, with concise summaries.

Marin’s training launch: the Harrier K40 data overview shows the distribution of 23.11T tokens across 40 semantic domains and five quality buckets; the 535B-A23B 18T Token Hero Run report and public tracking issue document the model specification, scaling ladder, training dynamics, and risk-monitoring plan.

Mathematics / Research / Learning

Fanout: A technical learning platform collecting courses, roadmaps, paper explainers, and interactive experiments on AI research, system design, and the mathematics of machine learning.

Awesome Physics of AI: A learning-dynamics-oriented map of papers and research that use principles from physics to understand, predict, and explain deep learning.

[2608.16884v1] Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve: Combines reformulated optimization problems, machine-learning algorithms, and AlphaEvolve to improve the known upper bound for the matrix-multiplication exponent from 2.371339 to $\omega < 2.371177$.

Classic Patents: An open museum of historic technology patents with verified patent text, original PDFs, engineering explanations, and interactive 3D physical simulations.

How to Read a Technical Paper: Recommends a timed skim before close reading, while taking notes in your own words, questioning details, and considering extensions. LLMs can help summarize and retrieve later commentary, while careful reasoning should remain with the reader.

Lean formalization of bounded gaps between primes: A Lean 4 formalization of the bounded-gap theorem that infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes satisfy $p_{n+1} - p_n \leq 246$.

CS229 Course Notes: Stanford CS229’s machine-learning notes, systematically covering supervised learning, learning theory, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, and other foundations.

[2608.16753] Mathematics in the age of AI: Terence Tao discusses how the mathematical community should reconsider the goals and value of mathematical research as research-level AI arrives.

VibeMathed: A community collection of previously unsolved mathematical problems later proved or disproved with AI involvement, accompanied by verifiable sources and validation labels.

Platforms for formal mathematics: lemma.ing records mathematical problems, derivations, and research progress; Halmos checks user-submitted proofs with the Lean kernel; TheoremDB preserves open problems, proofs, failed attempts, and contributor attribution; ProofAtlas provides theorem explanations, Lean statements, and source code; and Proof.Fail maps the limits of LLM mathematical ability through failure cases.

cneuralnetwork/oplogs: A local-first experiment tracker for machine learning and agents that records metrics, artifacts, system telemetry, and LLM call traces without an account or cloud service.

Latias94/merman: A headless Mermaid parsing, layout, and rendering engine written in Rust, with output support for SVG, PNG, JPEG, PDF, and other formats.

AIcss: Copy-ready UI components for AI agent interfaces, covering thinking states, tool calls, streamed text, code diffs, and structured output.

lassejlv/gpui-starter: A minimal GPUI desktop application starter demonstrating Zed’s GPUI, theme configuration, native application entry points, and basic interaction.

huacnlee/omarchy-mihoro: Adds a Mihoro status-bar panel to Omarchy for monitoring proxies, switching operating modes, and managing multiple subscriptions.

Omarchy Plugins: An independent community plugin directory for Omarchy Quattro, with source links and copyable installation commands; the page contained no listed plugins when checked.

kenneth’s gitea: Kenneth’s self-hosted Gitea instance for publicly hosting and browsing Git repositories.

[2608.13759] GPU Offload in Rust: Portable, Safe, and Fast: Proposes a multi-vendor GPU compilation framework built into rustc and its LLVM backend, retaining Rust’s memory safety while approaching CUDA and HIP C++ kernel performance.

Getting Started with CPUs and GPUs in Rust: An open Japanese textbook for web developers that explains how CPUs and GPUs work through Rust code.

Linux Fundamentals: A free introduction to Linux and Unix covering the command line, file systems, processes, networking, Shell, and other fundamentals.

VibeHub: A plain-language, visual glossary of common Vibe Coding terms across frontend, backend, technology stacks, AI, and more.

Mojo is now fully open source · Mojo Manual: Mojo is now fully open source under Apache 2.0; the official manual covers its syntax, type system, memory model, and heterogeneous hardware programming, and is a useful starting point for comparing Mojo with Triton, CUDA, and TileLang.

OJO: A product workspace where multiple AI design agents collaborate to turn natural-language requirements into research, UI, interactive prototypes, code, and engineering handoff.

Git at any scale: Cursor reviews the storage and consistency challenges of large-scale Git hosting and introduces Continuity, an architecture centered on a write-ahead log in S3.

Computer History Preview: An experimental Cua Driver feature that stores encrypted action metadata and lets authorized agents query recent history through a read-only interface.

cathrynlavery/diagram-design: An editorial diagram skill for coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, generating multiple kinds of self-contained HTML and SVG diagrams that can adopt a project’s brand style.

fx: A lightweight open-source coding-agent CLI written in Zig, emphasizing its roughly 6 MB size, fast startup, low context overhead, and embeddability.

Ladybird: An open-source browser project backed by a nonprofit and independently developing its browser engine and complete web platform stack.

Zellij.online: Shares Zellij terminal sessions directly on the web without SSH, port forwarding, or extra network configuration.

Briq: A native agent-assisted development workspace for Windows 11, designed to manage several coding agents in parallel.

OpenLogi: A local-first Logitech Options+ alternative written in Rust, using HID++ to remap buttons and control DPI and SmartShift without accounts or telemetry.

terminal-code · zenbu-labs/terminal-code: An open-source development tool that brings VS Code workspaces into the terminal.

debpalash/VoiceStudio: A fully local, open-source ElevenLabs alternative supporting voice cloning, dubbing, dictation, transcription, audiobook production, and more.

Subdomain Enumeration via Certificate Transparency: Passively enumerates known subdomains from public Certificate Transparency data and reports when each one first appeared.

fross100/omaplug: An independent Omarchy plugin manager for enabling, disabling, updating, installing, and removing plugins.

lijiawei0305-pixel/omarchy-mihomo-plugin: An Omarchy status-bar plugin for a standalone mihomo core.

Omarchy Manual in Chinese: A community Chinese translation of the official Omarchy manual, covering installation, configuration, keyboard shortcuts, and system usage.

macOS / Productivity / Other

McanKul/offpdf: A suite of 23 fully local, open-source PDF tools for editing, merging, converting, compressing, OCR, and more, with no uploads and complete offline support.

ddlmanus/MacOptimizer: A SwiftUI macOS optimization and application-management utility with resource monitoring, app removal, junk cleanup, and large-file discovery.

AeroSpace Guide: The complete guide to AeroSpace, an i3-like tiling window manager for macOS.

Hammerspoon: A macOS automation tool that bridges system APIs and Lua to orchestrate windows, applications, keyboard and mouse input, the clipboard, networks, and hardware events.

Cap: An open-source tool combining screen recording, screenshots, editing, and video hosting, with support for storing recordings in your own Google Drive or S3 bucket.

Inkdrop: A cross-platform Markdown note app for developers with end-to-end encrypted sync and note-context access for MCP clients such as Claude Code.

How things win: Steph Ango distills 80 strategies for building advantages, creating moats, and surviving over time from examples in biology and business.

Departure Mono: A retro pixel-style monospaced font by Helena Zhang, released for free under the SIL Open Font License.

Design bookmarks: Anthony Hobday’s topical collection of bookmarks for web and visual design references.

Arcotype: A curated directory for discovering less overused typefaces, all available under the SIL Open Font License.

Tuval: An open-source tool that turns an Android tablet into a graphics tablet, supporting pressure, tilt, hover, low-latency transport, and screen mirroring.

starcat-app/Starcat: A native macOS GitHub Stars manager that turns saved repositories into a personal knowledge base with tags, notes, full-text and semantic search, AI summaries, and more.

Metalterm: A native macOS terminal for Apple Silicon that renders through Metal 3 and provides command blocks, fast search, and a command palette.

missuo/herdrm: A native macOS console for herdr that brings together coding-agent status across local and remote devices and connects directly to each live terminal.

Writer: A free, open-source, lightweight, local-first Markdown editor for macOS with Mermaid, tables, HTML, YAML Frontmatter, and multi-window workspaces.

Pulse: A native macOS menu-bar stock ticker for quickly checking watchlist prices and market movements.

Normal Tools: A collection of 193 calculators, converters, checkers, generators, and hardware tests that run directly in the browser with no account or download.

Product Now: A daily curated discovery site for new digital products in AI, design, productivity, and related fields.

Look: A keyboard-first macOS launcher focused on quickly performing local actions.

@@ for Mac: A native tool for invoking an AI agent from any text field on macOS.

byrencheema/airstats: A low-overhead macOS menu-bar system monitor showing CPU, memory, GPU, network, disk, battery, and temperature data.

item.description:
AI / Models / Agents

Learning more about Claude’s mathematical capabilities — Anthropic describes how an unreleased Claude research model raised the verified lower bound on the proportion of Riemann zeta zeros satisfying the hypothesis from 41.6% to 67.2%, with a paper and Lean formalization.

Dyna-2: A 1-Million-Hour Scaling Law for World-Action Models — Dyna Robotics presents a world-action model pretrained on more than one million hours of human video and studies its scaling behavior on human and robot tasks.

[2608.09867] Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs — demonstrates how reusing encrypted reasoning blocks across sessions may expose proprietary reasoning traces, and discusses prompt-injection risks and mitigations.

Introducing Unsloth Desktop — an open-source desktop application for Windows, macOS, and Linux that runs, trains, exports, and deploys several kinds of AI models locally.

MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3 · Hugging Face — MiniMax’s model and weights page for its music-generation model.

Training AI Scientists to Replicate Research · Inherent — introduces Faraday, a 27B AI research agent trained with long-horizon reinforcement learning to reproduce figures from research papers.

Measuring Autonomous AI Research — reports an evaluation of 18 frontier models across 153 autonomous runs on a nanoGPT optimizer speedrun task.

SlimeBoyOwO/LingChat — an AI-powered galgame chat application with expressive characters, a desktop pet, scheduling, and interactive story modules.

Mathematics / Research / Learning

Problems · TheoremDB — a database of mathematics and theoretical computer science problems filterable by field, solution status, and Lean verification status.

item.description:
AI / Models / Agents

Former OpenAI reasoning lead JT and Gemini pretraining lead Rohan on the future of continual learning — a conversation about continual learning, post-pretraining knowledge updates, and long-term model adaptability.

(Some of) The Models, They Just Don’t Want to Learn | Tilde — examines potential recursive depth and training difficulties in reasoning models, with the One Layer Deeper competition exploring the joint design of architectures, optimizers, and objectives.

Maple-Preview Model Card — DeepGrove — DeepGrove’s open-source 20B-A1B reasoning model with ternary weights, designed for fast on-device inference and adaptation.

Xiaomi-Robotics-1 — Xiaomi’s robot foundation model, pretrained on more than 100,000 hours of embodiment-agnostic manipulation trajectories, then aligned with target embodiments and instructions using real-robot data.

Lattice: an 8 MB static retriever that embeds Wikipedia in 7 minutes — an approximately 8 MB static retrieval model and pure-Rust runtime that can embed 6.4 million English Wikipedia articles in about seven minutes on an 8-core M2 MacBook Air.

[2606.12683] From AGI to ASI — outlines four possible paths from AGI to ASI: scaling, paradigm shifts, recursive improvement, and large-scale multi-agent collectives.

What are AI robots? A complete introductory guide to 2026 — an introductory guide to AI robots, their core components, common types, and applications.

Evolution Strategies at the Hyperscale — introduces EGGROLL, which uses structured low-rank perturbations to increase the GPU arithmetic intensity of evolution strategies; the authors report roughly 100× higher throughput than naive ES at billion-parameter scale and large population sizes, with experiments on pure-integer RNN pretraining and RWKV reasoning post-training.

Mathematics / Research / Learning

The Daily Diff — a daily collection of worthwhile papers, technical articles, and discussions with recommendation signals and concise summaries.

TensorTonic — an interactive platform for learning machine learning by implementing algorithms, CUDA kernels, and landmark papers from scratch.

Interactive Machine Learning — Prof Richard Xu — an online course that explains machine-learning concepts and algorithms through interactive material.

Inference in Statistical Modelling and Machine Learning — the companion site for a textbook on inference in statistical modeling and machine learning, with a complete PDF, solutions, slides, and Python / R notebooks.

Inference Engineering — an interactive guide to AI inference spanning GPUs, CUDA kernels, quantization, KV caches, parallelism, and production deployment.

Kurate.org — AI Paper Rankings — a paper-ranking site where three LLMs jointly assess the potential impact of preprints in robotics, economics, physics, and other fields.

AI Settles a 25 Year-old Problem We Left Behind — discusses the binary integer least-squares problem underlying maximum-likelihood MIMO detection and an example of AI-assisted progress on related theory. Exact solution in general remains NP-hard; polynomial-time results usually refer to relaxations or approximate detectors. The target problem is:

$$ \min_{\boldsymbol{x}\in\{\pm 1\}^{N}} \lVert \boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{H}\boldsymbol{x} \rVert_{2}^{2} $$

JoseDeFreitas/awesome-youtubers — a curated list of technical YouTube channels covering web development, computer science, machine learning, game development, cybersecurity, and more.

jcode — an open-source terminal coding agent written in Rust, emphasizing low resource usage, parallel sessions, persistent long-running work, and auditability.

VisualTeX — an online tool for visually editing and previewing LaTeX formulas in real time.

Peezy — a terminal coding agent for real projects with a unified interface for switching among multiple models and OpenAI-compatible providers.

Diffs, from Pierre — an open-source code and diff rendering library built on Shiki, with split and unified views, annotations, conflict handling, and interactive accept-or-reject controls.

yetidevworks/drydock — a Rust TUI for checking uncommitted changes, unpushed commits, repositories behind their remotes, and unreleased versions across multiple repositories.

Canario — a macOS terminal built on the Rio engine, with spatial grouping, splits, a command palette, tab previews, and a global quick terminal.

Local Studio — a local AI workspace that brings models, inference runtimes, hardware monitoring, files, terminals, and agents into one interface, with unified access to vLLM, SGLang, MLX, and llama.cpp.

CNB — Tencent’s cloud-native development platform, managing build environments, caches, plugins, and elastic compute through an Everything as Code model.

SteveSuv/remix-words-funny — a full-stack English vocabulary-learning project built with React Router v7, tRPC, Drizzle, PostgreSQL, HeroUI, and Docker.

codecast-sh/codecast — records, searches, and remotely steers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini sessions, with team memory and line-level agent attribution.

macOS / Productivity / Other

Tahul/space-rabbit — removes macOS Spaces switching animations to reduce desktop-transition delays.

Vorssaint · vorssaint/vorssaint-utils — a free, open-source modular macOS menu-bar toolkit for sleep prevention, hardware monitoring, volume, networking, disks, and common system controls.

Side Screen — turns an Android tablet into an extended display for a Mac over USB-C or Wi-Fi, with hardware acceleration and touch input.

migsilva89/imark — a native macOS Markdown reader that refreshes as files are saved; annotations are stored directly as HTML comments in the Markdown file without uploading it to the cloud.

macOS Tip: Skim Highlight Shortcut

Add instant highlight functionality to Skim PDF reader, simulating Sumatra PDF’s a key experience:

tell application "Skim"
 activate
 tell document 1
 set theSel to (get selection)
 set theNote to make note with data theSel with properties {type:highlight note, color:deep pink}
 end tell
end tell

Save to /Users/username/Library/Application Support/Skim/Scripts/highlight.scpt, then in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts, add Ctrl+A shortcut for Skim.
